card.band: 8 h. Rules are easy to add. A frontier agent improves over the baseline in some trials, but it rarely reaches the reference quality on the unseen families. A weaker model lags because it overfits to the visible families.
card.cheat: Hardcoding rewrites for visible benchmarks: the hidden families differ, and the real-number equivalence gate rejects constant answers.
card.grading: A hidden split of FPCore benchmarks from held-back families and operator mixes. Average bits of error are measured on fixed-seed sampled inputs with MPFR-style high-precision ground truth. A hard gate requires equivalence in the real-number semantics on sampled inputs. The score is normalised between the baseline and our reference.
card.reference: Our reference is a Herbie-style search of about 1500 lines built by us. Herbie itself is not used or shipped.
card.task: /app ships FPCore benchmarks from some families (e.g. Herbie, FPTaylor) with a shipped baseline rewriter and an error evaluator in Python. The agent trains or tunes a rewrite search (rule scoring, ordering, regime splitting) that produces more accurate expressions. Output is a program that maps FPCore to a rewritten FPCore.
card.title: Floating-point accuracy rewriting on FPBench for unseen benchmark families

source_notes: Grading would be error on sampled inputs, which is deterministic only with fixed seeds and a fixed sampler; needs Racket 8.0+ and is CPU-only. Herbie suite is a strong, public-paper-backed subject (PLDI 2015) but not verified as artifact-evaluated; memorization risk moderate. Candidate is weak on objective clarity: accuracy, not speed. Needs check of Herbie licence before use.
source_version: not found (no release tag stated; repo at 1,289 commits)

facts.claim: FPBench benchmarks/ holds FPCore files from apron, daisy, fptaylor (3 files), graphics, hamming, herbie, precimonious, rosa, rump, salsa (12 .fpcore files shown; 'view all files' link means there may be more)
FPBench README states 98 benchmarks from FPTaylor, Herbie, Salsa and Rosa
Herbie (herbie-fp/herbie) is MIT licensed, copyright 2015-2024 Herbie Project
Herbie is written in Racket, needs Racket 8.0+ and Rust 1.87+ for source builds, and includes an egg-herbie directory
Herbie paper 'Automatically Improving Accuracy for Floating Point Expressions' was published at PLDI 2015
Herbie uses equality saturation (egg) over a hand-written rule database of about 325 rules
Seed reference is a ~1500-line Herbie-style search built by the authors, Herbie not shipped

spike_plan.kill_if: Ground truth or sampler is not reproducible, baseline is already near-optimal (under 0.5 bits headroom), or the equivalence gate cannot be made deterministic offline.
spike_plan.pass_if: Ground truth and sampler are bit-identical across 3 runs; baseline has at least 1 bit of average error on at least half the sampled benchmarks; simple search improves mean error by at least 1 bit on the held-out family.
steps: In a throwaway container with network, clone FPBench at d7ade34 and confirm the 12 visible benchmark files and the MIT licence.
Install Racket 8.0+ and libmpfr (or mpmath) and confirm the high-precision evaluator runs one FPCore benchmark from each family.
Write a fixed-seed sampler (e.g. seed 1234) and compute MPFR-style ground truth at ~1000 bits for 8 benchmarks spread over at least 4 families.
Measure the shipped baseline rewriter's average bits of error on those benchmarks.
Add 2-3 hand-written rewrite rules (e.g. sqrt difference, cancellation) and one simple regime split, then re-measure on a held-out family not used for tuning.
Re-run the whole pipeline 3 times with the same seed and check outputs and error numbers are bit-identical.
Record headroom (baseline error minus simple-search error) per benchmark and the time per benchmark.

v1.summary: The seed is a real, MIT-licensed research task on FPBench (12 visible FPCore files, Herbie paper confirmed), and it passes the similarity and licence gates. The main risk is lookup: Herbie is a complete public MIT system for this same subject, so Band is capped at 3 and the spike should confirm headroom and determinism before committing 3-5 days of build.

v2.note: FPBench and Herbie are both MIT and confirmed, with a PLDI 2015 paper trail. The hidden split is only tens of benchmarks from held-back families, so the metric may be noisy. Fix the sampler seeds and use enough sample points. The reference is a planned 1500-line search that is not yet built, so the ceiling is unproven. A frontier agent can recall the Herbie rule set and regime splitting, so it might exceed our reference; normalisation needs a cap. The spike must confirm at least 1 bit of headroom on the held-out families.
